submission.name: ReadyCheck Voice
submission.tagline: Practice checking safety gear before a campus event shift
submission.inspiration: Student volunteers and event crews sometimes take on unfamiliar setup jobs where protective gear matters. We wanted a quick practice tool that can check a few visible items and explain what might be missing.
submission.what_it_does: ReadyCheck Voice lets a user choose a sample event scenario, then uses a camera view to look for items such as gloves, goggles, or a vest. It gives a spoken status and can play through a short training scenario; it is a prototype for practice, not an operational safety check.
submission.how_we_built_it: The app combines a FastAPI backend with a React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind interface. A YOLO11n model handles image detection, Gemini can draft scenario variations, and ElevenLabs voices the feedback; we also tried organizing example detection records in Databricks for later review.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The demo connects the camera, detection, and spoken feedback paths, but the detector can miss gear when lighting or camera angle changes. We also have a known issue where the spoken status can lag behind the latest frame, so the user may hear feedback for an earlier image.
submission.accomplishments: We are proud to have a working prototype that takes a camera image through detection and produces a spoken response. Building around a small vision model let us explore the whole interaction in the time available.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that a vision result needs clear limits and context before it becomes useful guidance. Gemini helped us draft scenarios, while ElevenLabs made the feedback easier to follow without watching every status label.
submission.whats_next: We would improve the detector with more varied examples, make the voice feedback track the newest frame, and add a clear review step for a supervisor. We would also test the interface with event staff before considering real use.
